correctness.rationale: The proof uses the published exact polygonal extension characterization, derives the sideline-intersection recurrence directly, and proves spectral rigidity analytically. The positivity conditions follow from 2q+1<m/2. Summation fixes the eigenvalue, and equality in the triangle inequality rules out every nonconstant root-of-unity Fourier mode. The conclusion that equal supports with equally spaced normals give a regular polygon is immediate from the tangent-half-plane representation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general extension characterization does not itself identify which higher extensions are homothetic, while the vertex-recurrence classification does not produce the support recurrence. The present implication requires combining equal normal spacing with the exact extension endpoints and then proving a new spectral collapse.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new theorem is not a special case of the published (1,1) conclusion because it includes every admissible q. It is also not an immediate instance of the vertex-recurrence theorem: deriving any applicable recurrence from the illumination hypothesis is the substantive missing step, and here the derived recurrence lives in support coordinates.
